headline: Maritime History and Backcountry Permit Management
reservation: All backcountry camping requires a pre-booked permit via Recreation.gov, often selling out months in advance for the summer season. Boat cruises and guided kayak tours are separate commercial entities; check their official sites for availability as these are the primary ways to see the cliffs.

days.title: Sandstone Cliffs and Painted Rocks

stops.name: Miners Castle
stops.detail: View the most famous rock formation in the park from paved overlooks that showcase the turquoise Lake Superior water.

stops.name: Munising Falls
stops.detail: Take a short, accessible walk to a 50-foot waterfall dropping over a sandstone ledge in a shaded canyon.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes; conditions vary with summer traffic
days.note: Miners Castle is the park's busiest site; morning visits provide the most reliable parking.

days.title: Dunes and Distant Shores

stops.name: Grand Sable Dunes
stops.detail: Climb these massive perched dunes for a desert-like experience hundreds of feet above the lake.

stops.name: Sable Falls
stops.detail: Descend the stairs to see the falls and explore the rock-strewn beach where the creek meets Lake Superior.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; rough daily travel allowance
days.note: Walking on dunes is physically demanding; ensure you have adequate water for the sand trek.

days.title: Coastal Hiking and Hidden Arches

stops.name: Chapel Rock
stops.detail: See the iconic sandstone pillar with a lone pine tree, a testament to the region's erosive power.

stops.name: Chapel Beach
stops.detail: Relax on the sandy shore after the hike, observing the massive scale of the surrounding cliffs.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours including unpaved road sections; conditions vary
days.note: The access road to Chapel-Mosquito is unpaved and can be rough; check rental restrictions for dirt roads.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: The Chapel-Mosquito parking lot is frequently full by 8 AM during the peak July and August window. Have a backup plan like Sand Point if you arrive later.

intel.title: Upper Peninsula Limits
intel.text: Expect zero cellular service along the H-58 corridor and most hiking trails. Carry a physical map or a dedicated GPS device for wilderness navigation.

intel.title: Gateway Filling
intel.text: Fuel up in Munising or Grand Marais, as there are no services along the 42-mile length of the Lakeshore. Supplies are limited once you enter the park interior.

intel.title: Biting Insect Season
intel.text: Stable fly and mosquito populations peak in June and July, particularly near the wooded inland trails. Consider August or September for a more comfortable hiking experience.

intel.title: Lake Superior Temperament
intel.text: Water activities are subject to immediate cancellation due to high surf or 'gales' even in summer. Check the marine forecast before heading to the boat launches.

plan.arrival: Fly into MQT and drive 45 minutes to Munising to check in; use this gateway city for boat tour check-ins and picking up regional park passes.
plan.vehicle: While H-58 is paved, many trailhead roads are gravel and prone to washboarding; check your rental agreement for coverage on unpaved surfaces.
plan.goldenHour: Sand Point offers a westward view over the water for sunset, though colors are highly dependent on Lake Superior's evening cloud cover.
